Boston University (BU) is mulling a proposal to offer a dedicated undergraduate degree in artificial intelligence (AI). The final proposal is currently pending administrative approval, said Mark Crovella, professor and chair of academics for BU's Faculty of Computing and Data Sciences (CDS).

According to a report by The Daily Free Press, BU's independent student newspaper, Crovella hopes the CDS will offer a bachelor's degree in AI, launching in the fall 2027 semester.

“[AI] is in the process of changing the world,” he told The Daily Free Press. “We need students who both understand the technology, can create the technology, but also know how to use it responsibly and how to ethically incorporate it into society.”

BU currently offers related programs, including a Bachelor of Science in data science (within the CDS), a Bachelor of Arts in computer science, and a residential Master of Science in AI, along with five online master's programs in AI.

BU's plan would feature two tracks within the major: one focused on building advanced AI models and another on applying AI across disciplines, with a strong emphasis on AI ethics.

If approved, BU would join a growing number of higher education institutions to offer a Bachelor of Science in AI. Several Massachusetts universities already offer AI majors, including Bentley University, Northeastern, Wentworth Institute of Technology, and MIT. This fall, Northeastern renamed its Bachelor of Science program in data science to a Bachelor of Science in AI.

Azer Bestavros, a computer science professor and associate provost for CDS, told The Daily Free Press that he believes AI education will become essential across careers, noting that AI is not a standalone field.
